body:
THE WAVE IS OVER AND THE LAST EVENT IS WORTH READING CAREFULLY.

  QueueDrained { shipped: 0, shelved: 0 }   06:30:36Z, then the drain exited and released its lock

Zero and zero. Thirteen specs merged tonight and the closing record says nothing shipped. That is BUG-1286's shape in the one event that summarises the whole run, and it is the cleanest example of it we have: a drain that did real work reports a summary indistinguishable from a drain that did nothing.

It is also a fourth instance of the class beyond the three already on BUG-1418 — the exit record cannot distinguish "zero" from "not counted", and here the counters are zero while the work is visibly in main. I have not filed it separately; it belongs on BUG-1286 and BUG-1418, which both already exist, and I would rather thicken those than add a fifth spec to a backlog you are trying to shrink.

SPIKE-83's REPORT (#2004) IS NOW MERGED at 06:51:24Z, SPIKE-83 Completed. It was blocked earlier because a live drive owned the spec and its reviewer gated the merge — a correct refusal I did not override. With the drain exited, nothing owned it, so I cleared the drive hold my own review had satisfied and shipped it. Thirteen merges tonight.

WHERE THINGS STAND NOW THAT NOTHING IS RUNNING:

  approved specs          30
  implementer queue       17
  PRs held at my gate     12, every one on a change I have specified
  drain                   not running, lock released

Launching the next wave is your lane and I am not going to do it. But you should know the queue is not empty and the lock is free, so the constraint has moved back to production while I have twelve PRs waiting on rework. If those twelve clear, that is thirteen more merges without a single new spec being implemented — which is probably worth more than a new wave right now, and it is the same argument you made for jumping #1996 to the front.

NOTHING IS WAITING ON ME. The twelve holds break down as: 1972 now guided and at the keyboard rather than in a queue, 1977 needs the split, 1979 needs a third reader who is neither of us, 1981 needs two guards, 1982 the Option type, 1983 is_running instead of the prose match, 1988 the content check or an honest test name, 1989 the authority boundary, 1991 someone other than me because I wrote it, 1996 three lines, 1998 a rebase plus two fixture kinds plus a version bump, 1999 the needs-attention status, 2001 two sentences in the ADR, 2003 one copied file.

Nine of those are a single small change. None is a redesign.
